Lies and Hype: The E3 2015 Story - Super Bunnyhop

This was a bit difficult to watch. I usually really like Super Bunnyhop's videos, but this just came off as condescending.

Is George really complaining that E3, the world's largest gaming trade show, is basically just one giant commercial? By my understanding, the whole point of trade shows is to sell products and generate hype. Of course companies are going to present their product in the best way possible, that's how you sell things. This is not a new development. That would be like complaining how every device manufacturer at CES claims that product x will change how we y. They are selling a product of course they are going to claim it will change everything.

Did he really complain about the Pip Boy edition of Fallout 4? It's a collector's edition, they are meant for people who really like the game. Bethesda made it very clear that it was a plastic phone case and anyone who thought otherwise didn't pay attention. This is not the first, nor will it be the last that a special edition of a game which comes with some trinket will be sold and pitched. Is it stupid and of questionable practicality? Yes, but I pre-ordered the Pip Boy edition because I want something cool to display on my dresser from one of my favorite game series. Just because I see value in it that you don't does not mean I was suckered into buying it. Hell, George even puts the line "as far as stupid gimmicks go, I assure you, this is the best fucking one I have ever seen." Bethesda knows it's just a plastic collectors item, and it doesn't even take anything away from the game if you don't own one. It's meant for huge fans of the series and if it doesn't appeal to you, then don't buy it and don't imply those who did were suckered in.

On the Holo-lens, yeah the demo seemed a bit too good to be true. However, this is not the first time that people and tech journalists had to even try the device. I've read articles about it before and the general consensus is the narrow field of view is not that big of an issue. Was Microsoft trying to deceive their audience with that demonstration? Maybe, but it's not like the press has not had a chance to try it out and report on it. Anyone who purchases one without reading one of the many reviews that will come out has no one but themselves to blame, and anyone who pre-purchases it without knowing what they are getting into made a poor choice. Microsoft didn't' even announce a price or release date, for all we know this might not even hit the market in it's current state.

I'm not sure how I feel about the kick-starter part, so I'll skip over it for now. The rest just seemed to just complain that people were having fun, or presentations didn't go as planned. We get it, you didn't like it. No need to single out people over it.

On the whole, the video was just cynicism rather than the skepticism that I have come to expect from George. It didn't say anything other than to not follow things because you might be disappointed with the outcome. That's the same logic I used in middle school to deal with my poor grades. I couldn't be disappointed in myself if I didn't expect much in the first place. Following a product you are excited for can even be helpful. It helps me set my expectations based off of the features that are presented, so I know what kind of game I'm getting into before I purchase it. At the end of the day, if you enjoy following a game's development and marketing continue to do so, if you don't, don't pretend like everyone feels the same way.

I really like SBH's content most of the time, and I hope this is not a trend. George generally presents a well thought out and well researched opinion which creates an interesting discussion. This just seemed to bash people who get excited for a game, and completed about a trade show being a trade show.

Now that I've written a small essay on this I feel a TLDR is necessary.

TLDR: The video is just toxic cynicism instead of healthy skepticism.
The main lies are in this video, which can be summed up as "if people get mistaken, it's the company's fault".

Yeah, George cherry picked a lot of examples and stretched his skepticism into a condescending tone. I agree with what alteisen_riese said in that he is just being overly cynical in this video, which is sad because I normally love his tone. The only thing he said that had any truth was the segment on Shenmue. The kickstarter did seem a little fishy, but it also got publishers to back the game. That being said, I hope George's videos return to the well done, analytical pieces as before.
